about: A self-hosted app for families to track food, exercise, water and health together.

prs.title: Whole stones and feet no longer come back one short
prs.broken: With weight in stones and pounds, 13 st showed as 12 st 14 lb, and typing in the pound box added to the 14. Height had the same problem: 6 ft showed as 5 ft 12 in.
prs.changed: The conversion back from kilograms and centimetres now rounds to the shown precision before splitting into stones and pounds, or feet and inches.
prs.matters: People who track in stones or feet see the number they typed, and the boxes behave as expected.

prs.title: Body measurement exports use your units
prs.broken: The body measurements CSV labelled its columns in pounds and inches but wrote the stored kilograms and centimetres.
prs.changed: Each value is now converted to the user's units before export, the same way the on-screen table does it.
prs.matters: People who track in pounds and inches get an export that matches what they see.

prs.title: Oxford BMR now uses the right equation for each age
prs.broken: The Oxford calorie formula used one equation per sex at every age, and the female one was wrong, so older users got a resting calorie burn that was too high.
prs.changed: It now picks the published equation for ages 18 to 30, 30 to 60 and over 60.
prs.matters: A 65 year old woman of 60 kg now sees 1177 kcal instead of 1331, so her daily target is right.
